title: THE BILLIARD ROOM
comment: Accepted plate 989601, 2026-11-07. The camera follows the paint: cornice and wainscot lines meet at (.494, .268), and the table's height gives eye 1.27 adults. The marks here are not the level's: levels/billiards.json holds them, checked against the painted floor in its own test. Floor painted by the model and kept: the owner likes it.
scene: It is the mansion's private billiard room at night: a grown-up, intimate room of dark green and old wood, lit low over two billiard tables.
keep: every wall edge, pilaster, both billiard tables, the far doorway and the horizon

floor.layout: a dark wooden floor, one even tone across its whole area out to every edge of the picture, with the same grid as image 1.
floor.paint: The floor is plain dark polished wood, one even tone from end to end, lying open and clear down to the bottom edge of the picture.

panel.layout: dark green wall panels above dark carved wood wainscot, with a deep moulded cornice.
panel.paint: The walls are deep bottle-green panels with thin old-gold mouldings above a dark carved wood wainscot, with framed old sporting prints in small gilt frames, small brass wall sconces and a deep moulded cornice, all in soft dim light.

door.layout: a tall doorway at the far end.
door.paint: A dark wood doorway at the far end, the same width and height as in image 1 with its foot on the same line, opens onto a dim warm corridor, seen only as soft amber depth.

pilaster.layout: carved dark wood pilasters on both walls.
pilaster.paint: Carved dark wood pilasters with brass capitals run along both walls.

stage.layout: two full-size billiard tables with green felt tops and heavy carved wooden legs.
stage.paint: Two full-size billiard tables stand empty and exactly the size of the blocks in image 1, with bright green felt tops, heavy dark carved wooden rails and legs, and a triangle of coloured balls on each.

lamp.layout: low green glass billiard lamps hanging over each table.
lamp.paint: A long low billiard lamp with green glass shades hangs on brass rods over each table, casting warm light on the felt.
